S + 2 = U + 3 = X + 4 = B + 5 = G

questions.question: Three of the following four number-pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the number-pair that is different from the rest.
questions.questionHtml: Three of the following four number-pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the number-pair that is different from the rest.
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

Second number = (first number)2 + 2

7 : 51 → 51 = (7)2 + 2 = 49 + 2 = 51

10 : 98 → 98 = (10)2 + 2 = 100 + 2 = 102 ≠ 98

8 : 66 → 66 = (8)2 + 2 = 64 + 2 = 68

13 : 171 → 171 = (13)2 + 2 = 169 + 2 = 171

Hence, ’10 : 98’ is odd one out.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 24 ÷ 12 - 6 × 6 + 2 = 18
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

24 ÷ 12 - 6 × 6 + 2 = 18
questions.solution:
Interchanging ÷ and ×

24 × 12 - 6 ÷ 6 + 2

= 24 × 12 - 1 + 2 = 288 - 3 = 285 ≠ 18

Interchanging + and ÷

24 + 12 - 6 × 6 ÷ 2

= 24 + 12 - 6 × 3 = 24 + 12 - 18 = 18 = 18

Interchanging + and -

24 ÷ 12 + 6 × 6 - 2

= 2 + 6 × 6 - 2 = 2 + 12 - 2 = 12 ≠ 18

Interchanging × and +

24 ÷ 12 - 6 + 6 × 2

= 2 - 6 + 6 × 2 = 2 - 6 + 12

= 8 ≠ 18

Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All postcards are envelopes. No envelope is a paper. Conclusions: I. Some envelopes are postcards. II. No paper is an envelope. III. No postcard is a paper.
questions.questionHtml:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All postcards are envelopes.

No envelope is a paper.

Conclusions:

I. Some envelopes are postcards.

II. No paper is an envelope.

III. No postcard is a paper.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: All the conclusions, I, II and III, follow
options.html: All the conclusions, I, II and III, follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The best possible Venn diagram according to the information is as follows,

I. Some envelopes are postcards → True, as all postcards are envelopes, some envelope will definitely be the postcards.

II. No paper is an envelope → True, as no envelope is a paper.

III. No postcard is a paper → True, as postcards are envelopes, and no envelop is a paper.

Hence, all conclusions I, II and III follow.

questions.question: Which letter will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? P, U, R, W, T, ?, V, A, X
questions.questionHtml:
Which letter will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?

P, U, R, W, T, ?, V, A, X
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

P + 5 = U;

U - 3 = R;

R + 5 = W;

W - 3 = T;

T + 5 = Y;

Y - 3 = V;

V + 5 = A;

A - 3 = X

Hence, Y is the correct answer.

questions.question: The sum of the current ages of Asma and her grandfather is 80 years. 10 years from now, Asma’s age will be one-fourth of her grandfather’s age. What is Asma’s current age?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the current ages of Asma and her grandfather is 80 years. 10 years from now, Asma’s age will be one-fourth of her grandfather’s age. What is Asma’s current age?
questions.solution:
As per the question,

Let current age of Asma be X and that of her grandfather be Y.

Sum of their age = X + Y = 80       …(i)

Age 10 years from now,

X + 10 will be of Asma and Y + 10 of her grandfather, also given that

X + 10 = 1/4 (Y + 10)       …(ii)

From (i) X = 80 - Y put in (ii)

80 - Y + 10 = 1/4 (Y + 10)

90 - Y = 1/4 (Y + 10)

360 - 4Y = Y + 10

5Y = 350

Y = 70

Put Y = 70 in (i)

Therefore, X = 10

Hence, 10 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Before the 104th Constitutional amendment act 2020, under which article of the Constitution of India can members of the Anglo Indian community be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President?
questions.questionHtml: Before the 104th Constitutional amendment act 2020, under which article of the Constitution of India can members of the Anglo Indian community be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 331.

  • In January 2020, the Anglo-Indian reserved seats in the Parliament and State Legislatures of India were abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 
  • Om Birla is the 17th and current speaker of Lok Sabha.

Key Points

  • Under article 331 of the Constitution of India can members of the Anglo Indian community be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President.
  • Article 342 covers The Scheduled Tribes in India.
  • Article 330 deals with the reservation of seats of SCs and STs in Parliament.
  • Article 326 was amended in 1988 by the 61st Amendment Act, 1988. It lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.

Additional Information 

  • The Rajya Sabha should consist of not more than 250 members - 238 members representing the States and Union Territories, and 12 members nominated by the President. Each member is elected for a term of six years.
  • Jagdeep Dhankar is the current Chairman of Rajya Sabha and the present Vice-President of India.
  • 104th Constitutional Amendment Act ceased the reservation of seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative assemblies and extended reservations for SCs and STs for up to ten years.

questions.question: Dolly, the first cloned living being created at Roslin Institute in Scotland was a _______.
questions.questionHtml: Dolly, the first cloned living being created at Roslin Institute in Scotland was a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sheep. Key Points

  • Dolly was a female domestic sheep and the first mammal which was cloned on July 5, 1996.
    • She was cloned from an adult somatic cell through the process of nuclear transfer.
    • She was cloned at the Roslin Institute in Midlothian, Scotland, and survived there until her death when she was 6 years old.
    • Her existence was announced to the public on 22 February 1997.
    • She was originally code-named “6LL3,” but later on she was named after singer and actress Dolly Parton.
  •  Cloning
    • Cloning is the production of an exact copy of a cell, any other living part, or a complete organism.
    • Cloning of an animal was successfully performed for the first time by Ian Wilmut and his colleagues at the Roslin Institute in Edinburgh, Scotland.

questions.question: What is the value of all tangible resources such as raw materials and labour that are used in the production process called?

questions.solution:
• The value of all tangible resources such as raw materials and labour that are used in the production process is called real cost.
  • A fixed cost is that which does not change with a decrease or increase in the amount of services or goods sold or produced.
  • Opportunity Costs are the benefits that an investor or individual misses out when choosing one alternative over other.
  • Variable Costs are corporate expenses which change in proportion to production output.

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs. 4880 each, on one article the seller gained 22% and on the other he lost 20%. What is his overall gain or loss percentage, nearest to one decimal place?
questions.questionHtml: Two articles are sold for Rs. 4880 each, on one article the seller gained 22% and on the other he lost 20%. What is his overall gain or loss percentage, nearest to one decimal place?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer 3.4% loss

Key Points:

SP of each article = Rs. 4,880

CP of first article = 4,880 × [100/122] = 4,000

CP of second article = 4,880 × [100/80] = 6,100

Total SP of both article = 4,880 × 2 = 9,760

Total CP of both article = 4,000 + 6,100 = 10100

Total loss = 10,100 - 9,760 = 340

Loss percentage = [340/10100] × 100 = 3.36% ≈ 3.4%

Required percentage = [(124 - 115x)/124] × 100 = 7.25% ≈ 7.3%

In ΔOMB

questions.question: If \(\sqrt x - \frac{1}{{\sqrt x }} = 2\sqrt 2,\) then \({x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to∶

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

⇒ (√x - 1/√x)2 = (√x)2 + (1/√x)2 - 2

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 100 - 2 = 98

questions.question: Find the value of 7.5 + (5.4 ÷ 4.5 × 2) - 8 × 4 ÷ 3.2
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of 7.5 + (5.4 ÷ 4.5 × 2) - 8 × 4 ÷ 3.2
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below∶

Step-1∶ Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,

Step-2∶ Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

Step-3∶ Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

Step-4∶ Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.      

⇒ 7.5 + (5.4 ÷ 4.5 × 2) - 8 × 4 ÷ 3.2

⇒ 7.5 + (6/5 × 2) - 8 × (1/0.8)

⇒ 7.5 + 2.4 - 10

⇒ 9.9 - 10

⇒ -0.1

questions.question: If a + b + c = 6 and a 3 + b 3 + c 3 - 3abc = 126, then ab + bc + ca is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 6 and a<sup>3 </sup>+ b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3 </sup>- 3abc = 126, then ab + bc + ca is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Given:

a + b + c = 6 and

a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = 126

Formula used:

a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b +c) [(a + b + c)2 - 3(ab + bc + ca)]

Calculation:

As we know,

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b +c) [(a + b + c)2 - 3(ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 126 = 6 [62 - 3 × (ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 126 = 6 [36 - 3 × (ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 3 × (ab + bc + ca) = 36 -21

∴  (ab + bc + ca) = 5

Additional Information(a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc) = (a + b + c)[a2 + b2 + c2 - (ab + bc + ca)]

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

questions.question: If the total production in three states in all six years is represented by a pie-chart, what is the central angle of the sector representing production in the year 2014. (to nearest whole number)?

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 40% are girls. The average weight of the whole class is 59.2 kg and the average weight of the girls is 55 kg. What is the average weight of the boys?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 60 students, 40% are girls. The average weight of the whole class is 59.2 kg and the average weight of the girls is 55 kg. What is the average weight of the boys?
questions.solution:
Total students in the class = 60

Average weight of class = 59.2 kg

Sum of weight of all class = 59.2 × 60 = 3,552

Number of girls in class = 60 × 40/100 = 24

Number of boys in class = 60 - 24 = 36

Average weight of girls is = 55

Sum of weight of girls is = 55 × 24 = 1320

Sum of weight of boys is = 3,552 - 1320 = 2232

Average weight of boys = 2232/36 = 62 kg

questions.question: Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a person reaches his office 18 minutes late than the usual time. His usual time in minutes is∶
questions.questionHtml: Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a person reaches his office 18 minutes late than the usual time. His usual time in minutes is∶
questions.solution:
Concept Used:

As we know,

Time is inversely proportional to speed.

Calculation:

Let the usual speed of the person be 4x

And, Speed of the person after decreasing = 3x

Ratio of usual speed to after decreasing = 4x ∶ 3x

Ratio of usual time to after decreasing = 3x ∶ 4x

Now, 4x - 3x = 18

⇒ x = 18

3x = 18 × 3 = 54 min

questions.question: In ΔABC, P is a point on BC such that BP ∶ PC = 3 ∶ 4 and Q is the midpoint of BP. Then ar(ΔABQ) ∶ ar(ΔABC) is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, P is a point on BC such that BP ∶ PC = 3 ∶ 4 and Q is the midpoint of BP. Then ar(ΔABQ) ∶ ar(ΔABC) is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Given, BP ∶ PC = 3 ∶ 4

Suppose BP = 3 unit and PC = 4 unit

BC = BP + PC = 3 + 4 = 7 unit

If Q is the midpoint of BP, then BQ = QP

BQ = BP/2 = 3/2 = 1.5 unit

ar ΔABQ ∶ ar ΔABC = BQ ∶ BC

ar ΔABQ ∶ ar ΔABC = 1.5 ∶ 7 = 3 ∶ 14

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 132° at the center of the circle. Chord AB is produced to point P. Then ∠CBP is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 132° at the center of the circle. Chord AB is produced to point P. Then ∠CBP is equal to∶
questions.solution:
As we know

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the size of the angle subtended by the same arc at the circle circumference

Take any point Q on the circumference and join AQ and QC.

∴ ∠AOC = 2 × ∠AQC

⇒ ∠AQC = 1/2 × ∠AOC = 1/2 × 132° = 66°

Now, ∠CBP = ∠AQC   [Exterior angle of cyclic quadrilateral]

⇒ ∠CBP = 66°

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. "Unless you did not do your homework you will be punished," said the teacher.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

"Unless you did not do your homework you will be punished," said the teacher.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Unless you did not'.

Key Points

  • "Unless" already introduces a condition negating the need for "not."
  • Thus, in the given sentence "did not do" will be replaced with "do"
    • Correct sentence-  "Unless you do your homework you will be punished," said the teacher.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ASSIST

ASSIST
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

Assist means help (someone), typically by doing a share of the work.

Mend means repair (something that is broken or damaged).

Create means bring (something) into existence.

Change means make or become different.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. If the mixture becomes too thick add more milk. B. Finally, add sugar and nuts, and your kheer is ready. C. Boil milk in a heavy-bottomed pan and add rice. D. Cook for about twenty minutes stirring every once in a while till the mixture thickens.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. If the mixture becomes too thick add more milk.

B. Finally, add sugar and nuts, and your kheer is ready.

C. Boil milk in a heavy-bottomed pan and add rice.

D. Cook for about twenty minutes stirring every once in a while till the mixture thickens.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

The given process is the recipe for kheer.

Clearly, first should be C as we need to boil milk and add rice. Next should be D as it states for how much time it should be cooked. A tells what to do to make it drinkable. Clearly B is the final step. 

The correct sequence is CDAB.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. ACQUIT
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

ACQUIT
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Acquit means free (someone) from a criminal charge by a verdict of not guilty.

Evict means expel (someone) from a property, especially with the support of the law.

Convict means declare (someone) to be guilty of a criminal offence by the verdict of a jury or the decision of a judge in a court of law.

Forgive means stop feeling angry or resentful towards (someone) for an offence, flaw, or mistake.

Clear means easy to perceive, understand, or interpret.

questions.question: Choose the option that is the active form of the sentence. It was decided by the members that the report would be placed before the Chairman for his comments.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the option that is the active form of the sentence.

It was decided by the members that the report would be placed before the Chairman for his comments.

options.text: The members decided to place the report before the Chairman for his comments.
options.html: The members decided to place the report before the Chairman for his comments.

options.text: The Chairman decided to place the report before the members.
options.html: The Chairman decided to place the report before the members.

options.text: Did the members decide to place the report before the Chairman?
options.html: Did the members decide to place the report before the Chairman?

options.text: The Chairman's comments were to be placed on the report of the members.
options.html: The Chairman's comments were to be placed on the report of the members.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

The members should be the subject in the active form of the sentence. Would be placed is used that means the action will take place. So, option 1 is correct.

Option 2 changes the meaning of the sentence.

Option 3 is an interrogative sentence which is incorrect.

Option 4 is incorrect because the sentence does not talk about placing the chairman's comments but of placing the report.
